description: Build a reproducible database of railway stations, route records, and map layers from the local China railway CSV and HOTOSM GeoJSON datasets.
steps: Run ./init.sh from the ChinaHSR_Simulation folder
Verify station-data.json contains thousands of stations with WGS84 coordinates
Verify route-data.json contains simulated HSR routes seeded by real train origin-destination records
Verify hsr-stations.geojson and hsr-rails.geojson are present for the Mapbox layers

description: Book real seats by station interval so a seat becomes available to another passenger after the previous passenger gets off.
steps: Quote a train trip between two stations
Confirm a booking and receive a ticket ID, seat ID, car, row, seat letter, and price
Verify overlapping bookings cannot use the same seat interval
Verify a later passenger can reuse the same seat after the first passenger alights

description: Calculate realistic ticket prices from distance, seat class, segment occupancy, booking horizon, peak demand, and service frequency.
steps: Quote the same route in second, first, and business class
Verify higher seat classes cost more than lower classes
Increase occupancy on a segment
Verify the high-demand quote is higher than the low-demand quote

description: Provide an interactive dashboard and Mapbox map showing stations, rails, moving trains, occupancy, pricing, bookings, and events.
steps: Start the Vite app
Verify the map renders railway and station layers
Verify live train markers update as simulation time advances
Use the booking panel to create a ticket
Verify dashboard statistics and event log update

description: Keep the project reproducible, testable, and safe by running data prep, tests, production build, and secret scanning.
steps: Run npm test
Run npm run build
Run rg "sk\\.ey" . and verify no Mapbox secret token is stored
Update handoff.md and agent-progress.txt with evidence

description: Run a 24-hour January 1 simulation with calendar surge demand, at least two trains per route per day, dynamically higher train counts and prices during surge periods, 5x passenger volume, optimized allocation, and smoother train animation.
steps: Open the app at http://127.0.0.1:5174/
Verify the header shows January 1 with a New Year travel surge label
Verify the simulation schedules thousands of trains with at least two trains per route
Verify passenger count exceeds 5x the prior 407,005-passenger baseline
Verify dashboard metrics expose demand surge, price surge, service range, and worker cadence
Verify the map uses smaller train markers and interpolated animation between worker snapshots

description: Persist a full-year, uncapped China HSR route-day service simulation in OceanBase and expose annual totals in the dashboard while the browser keeps detailed rolling-day seat allocation.
steps: Run npm run oceanbase:seed with OB_* environment variables for the local OceanBase Desktop tenant
Verify OceanBase contains station, route, stop, segment, simulation run, and daily route service tables
Verify the latest annual run covers 365 days and 438,000 route-day rows
Verify annual trains, passengers, and revenue have no cumulative cap
Verify the dashboard displays OceanBase annual totals and worker/table-count metadata
Verify the browser simulation can roll from January 1 to January 2 with a fresh detailed service day

description: Persist queryable outbound and return route variants in OceanBase, expose ordered station sequences for every route, and make trains reverse at terminal stations to return through the same stations in reverse order.
steps: Regenerate route-data.json and verify each route has an outbound and return route contract with ordered station names
Run the OceanBase seed in skip-db mode and verify the summary reports route variants, variant stops, variant geometry, and raw rail-track counts
Advance a train from origin to terminal and verify it changes to return direction instead of oscillating or completing permanently
Verify the return leg uses the same stations and segments in exact reverse order
Advance the train back to the original station and verify it completes only after the return leg

description: Load the local 12306.db snapshot into the Mac OceanBase Desktop tenant and run the browser simulation from OceanBase-derived ordered route contracts.
steps: Verify OceanBase Desktop is running locally and accepts writes
Migrate 12306.db into cr_12306_* OceanBase tables
Export stations and routes from OceanBase into the simulation JSON contract
Start the static server and request /api/oceanbase-simulation-data
Open the app and verify the topbar reports OceanBase 12306 as the active data source

description: Build simulation train paths from OceanBase rail-track graph data and validate station coordinates so trains follow ordered station-to-station rail paths without haphazard turns.
steps: Export routes from the local OceanBase 12306 tables
Validate raw station coordinates against static station data and linked track anchors
Trace consecutive station edges over cr_12306_railway_tracks and cr_12306_station_track_links
Verify there are no long ordered-stop straight fallbacks, >90 km coordinate hops, endpoint mismatches, or sharp backtracking hooks
Open the app and verify the OceanBase 12306 source still loads on the map
